correctness.rationale: The recurrence has characteristic polynomial \((3+2r)\xi^2-4\xi+1\). For \(r>1/2\) its roots are \(\rho e^{\pm i\theta}\) with \(\rho=(3+2r)^{-1/2}\) and \(\cos\theta=2/\sqrt{3+2r}\). Matching the backward-Euler starter gives \(z_n=\rho^n[\cos(n\theta)+\beta\sin(n\theta)]\), \(\beta=((1+r)\sqrt{2r-1})^{-1}\), hence a phase \(\cos(n\theta-\phi)\). Because \(0<\theta<\pi/2\), the first strictly negative term is exactly the first integer with \(n\theta>\pi/2+\phi\), including the zero-at-equality boundary. The repeated-root formula at \(r=1/2\) is positive. Expanding \(\theta\) and \(\phi\) at \(r=1/2+\varepsilon\) yields the stated \(\pi\sqrt2\) delay constant. Fresh exact-rational replay reproduced first-negative indices 42, 12, 5 and 3 at \(r=0.51,0.6,1,2\).
